measurement_contract: One GPU-owning worker creates the hidden window, device, effects and resources. The producer performs no GPU API calls or floating-point pose calculations; it copies immutable pose templates created by the worker.

Two explicit FREE/WRITING/READY/READING/DONE slots preserve publication/collection order. Each payload contains 1382424 bytes: 7200 six-bone palettes plus six header values. The worker copies palettes into its private fixture objects.

Direct mode queues a 24-byte descriptor and uses the existing pose generator on the worker. It avoids palette copies and provides the closer no-copy fixture baseline, with descriptor/wait overhead included.
Serial-copy and pipelined-copy modes use identical snapshots and rendering. Each sample includes eight completed packets (four regular/extra pairs); mode order rotates through all six permutations.

Owned mode skips full-payload hashing only during timings; all pre/post image, state, ownership and deliberate alias controls retain it. Checked mode includes full checksum costs at publication and before/after rendering.

Preparation includes template-to-scratch and scratch-to-slot copies. Worker time includes palette application, rendering, actual GPU completion and any enabled integrity checks. Queue age sums publication-to-worker-start delays; it is not additional completion time.
Backpressure/collection waits remain in total completion. There is no inserted fake simulation work and no FPS estimate from enqueue cost.
findings: Four owned-mode runs need 0.7024-0.8115 ms of producer preparation per synthetic pair, excluding queue waits. This measures fixture copies, not native game-data capture.

Owned-mode paired completion savings against direct rendering are -0.2633/-0.1288 ms lit and -0.6285/-0.2262 ms shadow. The worker handoff does not make rendering faster; its potential value is moving work off the caller while preserving bounded ordering.

Pipelining saves 0.5338-0.7572 ms against the copied-but-immediately-waited baseline. That baseline adds work the original renderer does not perform and is not sufficient evidence of a game improvement.

Full-payload checksums increase producer preparation to roughly 3.3 ms per pair and add roughly 5.9-6.0 ms completion overhead against direct rendering. They are diagnostic work, not a required gameplay feature.
All checks pass before and after sustained reuse. Copy isolation, a deliberately borrowed scratch buffer, two-slot capacity, strict sequence and post-frame state are exercised.
limits: Synthetic 256x256 lit/shadow passes with fixed geometry/resources and an optimistic bulk-after-second instancer; no complete native beta.13 path.
Native material-source execution, live palettes/camera/visibility capture, texture/effect/resource lifetimes, heterogeneous materials and unsupported fallback remain unqualified.
Material generation/clock are synthetic scalar inputs; the packet does not yet serialize arbitrary native material values or resources.
Device/window creation on the worker is a fixture arrangement. It does not prove how to transfer rendering from the live game window/device owner or handle Reset/loss/destruction.
No terrain, reflections, UI, Present, real simulation/network/input work or full-frame timing. Separate lit/shadow times cannot be summed into a game FPS prediction.
The initial two-mode pilot lacked a no-copy baseline and is superseded; its log/hash are preserved below, with no use in the final decision.
